control_flow: In followLine: if the line tracker reads below 30 %, curve left; else if it reads above 70 %, curve right; else drive straight.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line to its end.

decision_points.condition: the line tracker's brightness: first below 30 %, second above 70 %

branches.outcome: above 70 % (white band or peach floor): it curves right

branches.reason: A reading between 30 % and 70 % exists only for an instant right at the edge of the black core, so the 60 frames a second may never see it.

equivalence_classes: beside the line, on the white band
input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: On black it curves left (7 % / 22 %), on white it curves right (22 % / 7 %)
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line, or on the white band beside it, in bright light, with line ahead
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then white, again and again
scenarios.title: Follows the line to its end
assumptions: The end of the line is where it should get to.

uncertainties: The reading between 30 % and 70 % only exists for an instant at the edge of a black line, so it may never be seen.
The line tracker's light % is the floor's brightness, not the room's light: a tunnel's dim light changes nothing it reads.
The program reads no obstacle sensor, so it can't stop at a wall or box.
Your sentence doesn't say where the line ends or what the robot should do there.
